newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures down on pre-holiday squaring.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures down on pre-holiday squaring.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished easier on Friday as players squared positions and took profits ahead of a long weekend in Japan.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract ended 280 points lower at 20,575 on light volume of 11,000 lots.
Dealers said turnover was depressed on the Tokyo bourse as participants were preoccupied with the launch of individual stock options trading.

A comment by Ministry of International Trade and Industry Minister Shinji Sato that Japan's policy of keeping interest rates low was not effective could also have been a dampening factor, dealers said.
"People have just squared off before the holiday. We've seen a good performance on the market in the last two days," a trader at a local institution said.
He said the September Nikkei should now be supported around 20,100-20,250 with resistance seen above 20,600.
Dealers said the Dow's performance over the next two sessions was likely to provide a cue when trading of Nikkei futures resumes on Tuesday.
The July MSCI Taiwan futures contract ended 0.1 higher at 412.9 on volume of 1,517 lots.
